findings.description: Linear byte-by-byte parsing loops and standard exponent/mantissa decoding in RealPayloadDecoder are bounded by input substrate length
findings.code_snippet:
while eo:  # exponent
                e <<= 8
                e |= eo[0]
                eo = eo[1:]

            b = fo >> 4 & 0x03  # base bits

            if b > 2:
                raise error.PyAsn1Error('Illegal Real base')

            if b == 1:  # encbase = 8
                e *= 3

            elif b == 2:  # encbase = 16
                e *= 4
            p = 0

            while chunk:  # value
                p <<= 8
                p |= chunk[0]
                chunk = chunk[1:]
findings.reasoning: The while loops in RealPayloadDecoder (lines 547 and 564) and the exponent/mantissa calculations are strictly bounded by the input byte length. The loops advance by 1 byte per iteration (`eo = eo[1:]` and `chunk = chunk[1:]`) over a finite byte slice. In Python, bit shift and integer reconstruction over finite input bytes is linear O(N) operations. There is no unbounded recursion, exponential amplification, or infinite loop condition. In addition, univ.Real handles (p, b, e) tuples by converting via math.ldexp(p, e) or similar float operations, which raise OverflowError on out-of-range exponents rather than hanging CPU/memory. Therefore, this is not an exploitable denial-of-service vulnerability.

evidence.notes: Standard ASN.1 BER REAL decoding according to ITU-T X.690. Resource consumption is linear in input byte size. False positive.
evidence.code_context:
In pyasn1/codec/ber/decoder.py lines 545-568:
eo and chunk are bounded byte slices extracted from chunk (which itself is bounded by the length read from stream).
Each iteration of `while eo:` consumes one byte (`eo = eo[1:]`), meaning it executes at most len(eo) times.
Similarly, `while chunk:` consumes one byte per iteration (`chunk = chunk[1:]`), executing at most len(chunk) times.
The resulting tuple (p, 2, e) is passed to univ.Real, which stores it as a tuple or converts it to float via math.ldexp (which raises OverflowError if exponent is too large, rather than hanging or computing unbounded BigInts).
evidence.dataflow_analysis:
The data flow originates from incoming BER substrate bytes into RealPayloadDecoder.valueDecoder.
The loop terminates strictly after len(eo) and len(chunk) steps. No infinite loop or quadratic/exponential amplification exists.

flags.message: The loop strictly decrements input byte length on each iteration, guaranteeing termination without uncontrolled resource consumption or infinite loop.
flags.evidence: eo = eo[1:] and chunk = chunk[1:] ensure termination after len(eo) and len(chunk) iterations

sanity_check.reasoning: The loops in RealPayloadDecoder process finite byte sequences slice-by-slice, strictly advancing by 1 byte per iteration until exhausted. There is no possibility of an infinite loop (CWE-835) or uncontrolled resource consumption (CWE-400) beyond normal linear processing of the input payload.
